title: Geographic distribution of fatal car crashes, New York City 2016
method: Draw all 72 fatal collisions (2016; the file contains nothing else) as points sized by persons killed and coloured by borough, over the 5 NYC borough polygons, with geoplot in an Albers equal-area projection centred on NYC (both layers EPSG:4326 -> reprojected by geoplot/cartopy).
benchmark_defects: Mostly a cartographic task: the data are already filtered to 2016 fatal crashes, so 'analysis' reduces to drawing all points correctly located with the borough layer.
The published reference script calls main() only under an `if __name__ == '__main__'` guard.
checks: required: all 72 collisions drawn at their positions AND visible: visible drawn points (inside axes limits on plain axes; inside the set_extent/extent= frame from the code on cartopy/geoplot axes; all points when no extent is set) hold 71-81 distinct locations and >= 71 inputs match after min-max normalisation

required: the borough layer is drawn (a polyplot/choropleth/add_geometries/ShapelyFeature/<layer>.plot call resolved to a captured polygon layer or an inline read of nyc_boroughs, covering >= 95 % of the borough area; subsets excluded) and >= 90 % of drawn points lie in its expanded bounds in the CRS it is drawn in; no resolvable drawing call -> UNVERIFIABLE (not passed)

required (the text says 'plot ... on a map by geoplot'): crashes plotted with geoplot - a geoplot pointplot/kdeplot/quadtree/voronoi/webmap call in the executed code (aliases followed, comments ignored)
optional: fatalities encoded (size/colour by persons killed)

figure (kind="figure"; secondary analysis, never required): crash markers visible against a white background - >= 90 % of drawn markers whose colours are captured have face (or per-point edge) luminance <= 0.88 after alpha compositing; uniform colours not captured -> UNVERIFIABLE
